title: Controv. VII: Whether Christ's death is universal for all and each as to obtaining forgiveness
pass_a_gloss: VII. On the death of Christ as universal for all and for each — for the elect as much as for the reprobate — with respect to the obtaining of remission of sins, of righteousness, and of eternal life, provided they themselves do not place an obstacle: the matter returns to Controversy IV. See also the Articles with the Arminians, II, on the amplitude, object, and efficacy of Christ's death, and the first falsehoods there, pages 250, 251, 252.
pass_b_english: VII. On Christ's death as universal for all and each — elect and reprobate alike — as to obtaining forgiveness of sins, righteousness, and eternal life, provided they themselves do not put an obstacle in the way: the question returns to Controversy IV.
See also the Articles with the Arminians, II, on the breadth, object, and efficacy of Christ's death, and the first falsehoods there (pp. 250–252).
source_text: VII. De Morte Christi universali pro omnibus & singulis, tam electis quam reprobis, quoad impetrationem remissionis peccatorum, justitiae, & vitae aeternae, modo non ipsi ponant obicem, redit Controv. IV. Vide & Articul. cum Armin. II. de amplitudine, objecto, & efficacia Mortis Christi, ac πρῶτα ibi ψεύδη, p. 250. 251. 252.
notes: Controv. print p. 53 / PDF ~154. Margin De Morte Christi universali. Articul. II normalized from print 11. Cross-ref to Arminian articles pages only; Arminianismum body not densified.
